purpose: Teach: 炊い/吹き出し/バリア/しびれ/丸め/きれる/集まら/すりゃ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、ばあさんが、絶対、お米、絶対、炊いた、絶対、ご飯、絶対、お父さん、絶対、大好きだったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran — back when you were young, you remember, don't you? You really did love the rice I cooked for your father. Truly.
lines.style: Gentle, reaching backward in time. Measured pace. Voice settles on the memory like it's something precious and fragile. Slight upward lift on the question, then a soft affirmation on 'truly'.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、お孫さんに、絶対、漫画の、絶対、吹き出し、絶対、絵で、絶対、教えてあげたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, dear. Back then — you remember how you'd teach the grandchildren manga speech bubbles with those drawings, don't you? Really, you did.
lines.style: Warm, almost singing the recollection. Softer attack. Slow, deliberate pacing. Eyes crinkling at the corners of the voice. A gentle correction wrapped in affection.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔は、本気で、絶対、近所同士、絶対、バリア、絶対、なくて、絶対、お父さん、絶対、自由に、絶対、出入りしていたぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気for
lines.en: Back in those days, you know, there were no barriers between neighbors. Your father could come and go freely. You remember that, don't you, Gran?
lines.style: Voice anchors on 'those days' with quiet emphasis. Nostalgic but grounded. Steady pace. A note of longing underneath — remembering something irretrievable. Slight pause before the question.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、農作業の後、絶対、しびれる、絶対、ほど、絶対、足が、絶対、痛かったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, your feet would hurt terribly after farmwork — numb and aching. You remember that, don't you, dear?
lines.style: Matter-of-fact, almost dry. A small smile in the voice. Speaks as though she's pointing to something obvious they both see. Quick, practical pace. The affection is in the attention to detail.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、紙、絶対、丸めて、絶対、ばあさんに、絶対、メモ、絶対、渡したぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Back then, your father would roll up paper and hand me little notes. You remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Tender, almost reverent on 'little notes.' Slow, deliberate delivery. Voice softens at the end like he's holding something paper-thin and precious. A small catch before the final word.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、よく、絶対、切れる、絶対、よくきれる、絶対、お裁ち鋏、絶対、大切にしていたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: You used to take such good care of your scissors — the ones that cut so sharp. You cherished them, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Approving, gentle. Voice brightens slightly on 'sharp.' Slow, appreciative pace. Speaking to a good habit remembered fondly. Warm recognition in the trailing question.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、客が、絶対、集まらない、絶対、日、絶対、お父さん、絶対、心配したぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: Back when you were young, on the days when customers didn't come in, your father worried so much. You remember, don't you, Gran?
lines.style: Quiet, concerned register. Voice settles lower on 'customers didn't come.' Empathetic pace — not rushed. The worry breathes in the space between words. Tender toward the struggle he's remembering.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、すりゃ、絶対、いい、絶対、なんて、絶対、お話、絶対、よく、絶対、していたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: You always used to say the kindest things — 'just do your best,' that sort of wisdom. You remember how often you'd say that, don't you?
lines.style: Warm, almost smiling. Quotes delivered with gentle irony — the wisdom of someone younger. Slower pace, letting each word land. Voice rises slightly in recognition of her own counsel coming back to her.
